items.title: Arturo O'Farrill interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 6, 2024
items.q: I think of people who demanded that the truth tellers, that the truth be told, that Governor Faubus be called out.

ctx.x: At UCLA you were, or still are, the professor of Global Jazz Studies. And I wonder if that title, if you were in on that title. Because it’s not a common thing if you look at other colleges and their jazz department, it stands out that you call it “Global Jazz Studies.”

I actually created the Global Jazz Studies program first for Brooklyn College and then when I went to UCLA they already had a Global Jazz Studies program in place. So a lot of that is the realization that a lot of academia is making about the nature of jazz. In the first case we have to — this is not a popular position but I’ll go ahead and state it. Jazz is — we know this, it’s a verifiable fact — jazz is a word that was made up for a concert. It was put on a flyer and it was even denigrated — it was, I forget…

what it means to be American, which means to embrace multiplicity. The real definition of America is a nation borne out of many, many, many people. The nation was not founded by white Europeans, it was already here with indigenous beings and the indigenous people are the Americans who were already here. So the United States, the history of many people coming together to form this union. And that’s to me is what jazz is. Jazz at its best represents the multiplicity of cultures, the trans-culturation of humanity.…
